quick_skim.title: Managing Uncertainty in Teacher Vibe Coding: A Comparison of Teacher and Expert Workflows
quick_skim.abstract: Vibe coding, or natural language software development, enables teachers to become creators of digital teaching artifacts. However, novice educators oftentimes face different barriers. This qualitative study examined the workflows of pre-service teachers, in-service teachers, and expert developers through think-aloud protocols. Findings reveal vibe coding operates through a loop of problem framing, development, and verification governed by uncertainty management. Teachers reduced uncertainty by grounding designs in authentic needs: pre-service teachers drew on pedagogical principles, whereas in-service teachers relied on everyday teaching challenges. Conversely, Experts reduced ambiguity by constraining requirements, decomposing artifacts into testable modules, and automating tests. These differences reveal complementary forms of pedagogical, contextual, and technical expertise. Future work may be about supporting nontechnical teachers in developing reliable and educational applications.

quick_skim.title: Adesktop learning factory for smart and resilient manufacturing based on digital twin and AI
quick_skim.abstract: Learning factories have been increasingly applied in engineering research and education. In this paper, we develop a small-scale, low-cost, fully open-sourced learning factory that leverages AI and digital twins to demonstrate smart and resilient manufacturing. The learning factory consists of an AGV, three robots, two conveyors and their digital twins. Three typical use cases are designed to demonstrate the capabilities of the learning factory, i.e., material sorting through computer vision-based robot control, coordinating AGV, robots and conveyors for assembly, and digital twin-driven predictive maintenance. The results show that the developed learning factory can adequately support the teaching and research activities on digital twins and AI on manufacturing. Its fully open-source architecture and relatively low deployment cost make it an ideal solution for universities and research institutions.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: A small-scale, low-cost, fully open-source desktop learning factory with an AGV, three robots, conveyors and digital twins uses AI and digital twins to demonstrate smart resilient manufacturing across three use cases, supporting teaching and research.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 工程教育中的学习工厂往往成本高、难以复制，限制了其在教学中的推广。作者搭建了一个小型、低成本、完全开源的桌面学习工厂，由AGV、三台机器人、两条传送带及其数字孪生构成，结合AI与数字孪生演示智能韧性制造。研究设计了基于计算机视觉的物料分拣、AGV与机器人协同装配、数字孪生驱动预测性维护三个用例。结果表明该平台能有效支撑数字化制造的教学与科研活动，为工程教育提供可复制的开放实践平台。
